newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Nikkei futures end up, no sign of big gains.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Nikkei futures end up, no sign of big gains.

text.p: SIMEX Nikkei futures received a boost from some late short-covering on Tuesday but dealers said the market lacked conviction and was unlikely to head significantly higher ahead of the Bank of Japan's quarterly business sentiment survey next week.
They said reports the survey or "tankan" would not show significant signs of improvement, signalling the need for continued low rates in Japan, spurred some buying.
The benchmark Nikkei 225 December contract ended 25 points off its intra-day high of 20,990 against a previous settlement at 20,840.
"People don't want to be over-exposed in one direction ahead of the tankan," said a Japanese bank dealer.
He said uncertainty over the new Japanese cabinet and Japan's financial reform plans was also hampering interest.
The December Nikkei is likely to trade within a range of 20,800 and 21,300 for the rest of the week, he said.
